title: Scene description
description: A vision model's reading of one rendered SAR scene, validated and provenance-stamped (`umbra_py.describe.SceneDescription.to_dict`). Emitted by `umbra describe --json` and by the `describe_scene` agent tool (MCP / LangChain / LlamaIndex). Everything a model wrote is in `summary`, `observed_features`, `confidence` and `caveats`; everything else is filled in deterministically and cannot be overridden by a reply — which is the whole point of the document. A reader that quotes the text must carry `attribution` and `provenance` with it.

item_id.description: Which acquisition was read. Null when the description was produced from bytes rather than from a catalog item.

summary.description: The model's short plain-language paragraph about the scene. Model-authored: it is an interpretation of a picture, not a measurement.

observed_features.description: Short phrases naming what the model says it saw. Model-authored, and empty when it named nothing.

confidence.description: The model's own hedge on the reading, or null when it gave none (or gave one this does not recognise — an unrecognised level is dropped rather than passed through).

caveats.description: Short phrases qualifying the reading. Model-authored, plus the deterministic one a smaller picture adds: a baked preview is 512 px (the published sidecar) where a render defaults to 1024, and that caveat names what the model could not have seen at that size.

model.description: Which model produced the text, so a description can be attributed to it. Null when the caller injected its own describer (a test, or a local model with no identifier).

asset.description: The product the picture was made from.

attribution.description: The CC-BY line, which must survive into anything quoting the description (design principle 4: licence propagation is non-negotiable, including for model-generated text about the data).
examples: Contains Umbra open data, licensed under CC BY 4.0.

provenance.description: The fixed note saying this text is an AI interpretation rather than a measurement. Set by the library, never by the model, so it cannot be argued away by a reply.

image.description: Which picture the model was actually shown. Null only when no image record was captured (an injected renderer in a test).

sceneImage.description: The picture as evidence: where it came from and how big it really was. `width`/`height` are read from the PNG header, so they are what the model saw rather than what the call asked for — and they can disagree with `max_size`, which is exactly why both are recorded.

source.description: `rendered` — a fresh quicklook streamed from the COG for this call; `baked` — the cached preview from the local index (`umbra describe --preview baked|auto`), which costs no S3 read and no `[viz]` extra.

asset.description: The product the picture is of. For a baked preview this is what the index recorded the bake as, not what the request assumed — a bake of another product is refused by name rather than substituted.

width.description: The picture's real pixel width. Null only when the bytes are not a PNG this can measure; `source` is still recorded, since which cache a picture came from is the part a reader cannot recover afterwards.

height.description: The picture's real pixel height, null under the same condition as `width`.

max_size.description: The longest edge the call asked for. A baked preview will normally be smaller than this.

db.description: Whether the amplitude was stretched in decibels (the default) rather than linearly.
